package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware distributed via bundling/drive-by-downloads, not a package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: Fireball is a browser hijacker with remote control capabilities, designed to take over browsers, manipulate web traffic, and generate advertisement revenue. It is distributed without user consent, can execute arbitrary code, and enables large-scale ad fraud and potential further compromise of infected systems.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (upon browser launch or system startup)
execution_context.file_location: Injected into browser process or installed as a browser extension/add-on

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code modifies browser settings to set a malicious homepage and search engine, injects advertisements into web pages, monitors user activity, and executes remote commands received from a C&C server, resulting in browser hijacking, ad fraud, and potential further compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code takes control of browser settings without user consent, injects ads, and allows remote code execution, which are all hallmarks of browser hijackers and adware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal browser extensions or software should not change browser settings or execute remote code without explicit user permission.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise browser management tools may set homepage/search engine, but only with user/admin consent and without ad injection or remote code execution.

attack_chain.action: User unknowingly installs Fireball via bundled software or drive-by-download.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware is present on the system and can execute at browser launch or system startup.

attack_chain.action: Fireball modifies browser settings to hijack homepage and search engine, and injects ads.
attack_chain.leads_to: User web traffic is redirected and monetized by the attacker.

attack_chain.action: Fireball establishes communication with a remote C&C server and can execute arbitrary code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker can further compromise the system or use it for additional malicious activities.

behavioral_signatures: Unauthorized modification of browser homepage and search engine settings
Injection of advertisements into web pages not present in original content
Browser extension or process making unexpected outbound connections to ad or C&C domains
Execution of code received from remote servers
file_indicators: Presence of unknown or suspicious browser extensions/add-ons
Unexpected changes in browser configuration files (e.g., prefs.js for Firefox, registry for IE/Edge/Chrome)
Persistence mechanisms in startup folders or scheduled tasks
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known Fireball C&C or ad fraud domains
Frequent HTTP requests to domains not associated with user activity
Unusual traffic patterns from browser processes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unauthorized changes to browser settings (homepage, search engine), unexpected browser extensions, and outbound network connections to known malicious domains. Use endpoint security tools to detect browser hijacking behaviors and remote code execution attempts. Correlate browser process activity with network traffic to identify ad injection and C&C communication.
